title: content.analyzeReference
description: Computes the reference alignment data of a clip's reference binding as a job of kind referenceAnalysis, as OpenTune does when such a clip is selected: the alignment features of the clip placementId and of the clip it is bound to. AUTO in reference mode (content.autoTune) aligns with this data, and content.getDetails reports whether it exists (reference.alignmentReady). The placement needs a reference binding (else INVALID_ARGUMENT(reference_not_bound)), both clips need a finished pitch analysis (NOT_READY(f0_not_ready) while one runs), and a placement that does not exist gives NOT_FOUND(unknown_handle). A call for a placement for which a job that content.analyzeReference started is not terminal returns that job; it never returns a job that content.autoTune started, whose result has another shape (PROTOCOL.md section 12.1). The job checks again when it runs, before it stores anything, that the placement still exists (else NOT_FOUND(unknown_handle)), that it still has the same reference binding (else INVALID_ARGUMENT(reference_not_bound)) and that both analyses are still ready (else NOT_READY, with the reason of section 11); a job that fails stores no alignment data. When the alignment data does not exist yet and OpenTune's analysis does not complete, the job fails with NOT_READY(reference_analysis_stalled) (OpenTune completes one reference analysis per session; not retryable until OpenTune restarts), NOT_READY(reference_analysis_timeout) (the wait limit passed; retryable) or ANALYSIS_FAILED(reference_analysis_failed) (PROTOCOL.md section 12.6). The data is derived from the audio and changes no edit, so the method is not a write and creates no undo entry; the job's result (jobResult) names the binding and reports alignmentReady. Cancelling discards the analysis (PROTOCOL.md section 12.3).
